rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) allowable annual rent increase
rules.requirement: Rent for RSO units may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage. Rent may be raised to market rate after a voluntary move-out or certain evictions. Effective February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer add an extra percentage increase for utilities.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in the City of Los Angeles first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28. Covered types include apartments, condominiums, townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming/boarding house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes and RVs in mobile home parks.
rules.exemptions: For condominiums and townhomes, the rent amount is not regulated for tenancies that began after December 31, 1995. Rent may be raised to market rate when the tenant voluntarily moves out, is evicted for nonpayment, lease violation, failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan or a City Attorney order, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement. A landlord may apply for a Luxury Exemption.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: RSO additional tenant rent increase
rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, a 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. A 10% increase is allowed for an additional tenant who is not a dependent, and the landlord can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.
rules.key_value: 10% for an additional tenant (not a dependent)
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units).
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction, notice and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: RSO tenancies may be ended only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons. No-fault evictions require filing a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict, a 30-day or 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension), and payment of tenant relocation assistance. All termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
rules.key_value: 30-day and 60-day written notice; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_text: All rental units subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units). At-fault causes: failure to pay rent, lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar rental agreement, failure to provide reasonable access, unapproved subtenant at end of lease term. No-fault causes: owner or immediate family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition and permanent removal from the rental market, government order, conversion to affordable housing.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5; Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).
